newsitem.title: UK: Mark falls on EMU worries, Eurobourses down.
newsitem.headline: Mark falls on EMU worries, Eurobourses down.

text.p: The German mark dropped against the dollar and sterling on Monday , hit by jitters over the European single currency, and European bourses fell, preoccupied by domestic issues.

London stocks were well down as strong economic data revived fears of higher interest rates. Frankfurt, which made early gains, ran out of steam and floor trade ended with losses, with after-hours deals tumbling by over one percent.

The main action was in currency markets, where nerves over European economic and monetary union (EMU) drove the dollar up by almost a pfennig to 1.7465 marks, a 40-month peak, before it fell back slightly.
Sterling also rose to a five-year high against the German currency.

Traders moved in on safe haven currencies after a rift within German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling alliance over EMU widened at the weekend with one of his partners raising the prospect of leaving the coalition.
"We are continuing to see this structural desire to shift out of core EMU currencies into alternatives," said Shean Shepley, international economist at CS First Boston.
The German dispute pits members of Kohl's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) against its Bavarian sister party, the Christian Social Union (CSU), and above all Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber.

Stoiber is calling for a delay in monetary union if the entry criteria are weakened. He has threatened to block German membership of EMU in the upper house of parliament unless the criteria are strictly met.
"Europe has big problems to get over and the way the politicians are going about it is not very constructive," Shepley added.

The dollar eased back to 1.7420 marks, along with a weakening Wall Street, after a higher-than-expected reading in the Chicago Purchasing Managers Index for June and a rise in U.S. single-family home sales in May.

With the German currency already vulnerable over EMU, sterling was given an added lift, reaching 2.9042 marks, when stronger-than-expected British data on consumer credit fuelled chances of an interest rate increase.

In equity markets, London opened higher but turned negative to make sharp losses as --in contrast to currency markets-- the prospects of higher British interest rates had the effect of depressing stocks.
Investors were also becoming increasingly worried about the potential for bad news in the new Labour government's budget on July 2 amid talk that it could cut dividend tax breaks for pension funds.
"All these figures do is continue to excite the fear over the policy mix we are going to get," said Andy Hartwill, equity strategist at SocGen.
Hartwill said there was scope for a "relief rally" after the British budget, but that a poor economic backdrop for the second half made him cautious over the market's outlook.
The market was also likely to be edgy this week ahead of a meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's monetary policy-makers, analysts said.
Few expect an immediate U.S. interest rate rise but the U.S. central bank is likely to be alert for any signs that the underlying strength of the economy could feed inflation in coming months.
Frankfurt initially made modest gains, underpinned by the stronger dollar and Friday's Wall Street gains. But the blue-chip DAX index lost confidence and ended down 9.64 points at 3785.77.
Computer trading on the IBIS index fell more sharply, registering losses of 1.05 precent , perhaps depressed by Wall Street opening losses.

Paris shed its opening profits to make losses of 0.85 by midafternoon. Car-maker Renault fell 3.5 percent at 150.0 francs on profit-taking with brokers saying the closure of the Vilvoorde plant in Belgium, confirmed over the weekend, was priced into the share.
In bullion markets, gold was fixed in the afternoon at $334.55, up slighlty on the morning fix of $334.05 an ounce, its lowest for 4-1/2 years, under pressure from the strong dollar.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was at 114.30 yen and 1.7420 marks, compared with 114.62 and 1.7365 in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 31.9 points at 4,608.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 slipped 29.03 to 2,862.01 points.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 9.64 points at 3,785.77.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $334.55 an ounce against $337.15 at Friday's close. Silver was at $4.69, down five cents.
